title: Uncoordinated Cross-System Updates (Dual Writes)
pattern: Sequentially updating two separate, decoupled database systems or services in a single workflow without coordinating transactions.
why_bad: If the first write succeeds but the second write fails (e.g. due to a network outage), the system is left in an inconsistent split-brain state with no automatic way to roll back the first write.
detection: A single, uncoordinated controller method writes to a database and then makes an external, un-transactioned API call, without catching downstream exceptions and rolling back the database state.
counterexample: A system utilizing a transactional outbox pattern where the database update and the outbox message are committed in a single local transaction.
fix: Use asynchronous message queues combined with compensating transactions to undo the first write if the downstream service fails, or use event-driven reconciliation.
source: Scott Wlaschin, *Domain Modeling made Functional*, page 119 / passage [242, 534, 538, 539].
